families.mechanism: A prior 8-hour range boundary is swept intrabar and the completed bar closes back inside the range; enter opposite the sweep.
Low directional efficiency and weak EMA separation define balance; a two-standard-deviation close is faded toward the local mean.
An outsized range with a dominant body and extreme close is followed in the shock direction.
After a qualified shock, the next completed bar crosses back through the shock midpoint; enter opposite the original shock.
At a fixed UTC session transition, continue a prior session move only when net displacement is at least 60% of its range and the session closes in its outer 20%.
families.required_data: M15 Bid OHLC and UTC session clock

families.mechanism: Previous-day or Asian-session liquidity is swept and the bar closes back inside the reference range; enter the rejection.
families.required_data: M15 Bid OHLC and UTC day/session levels

families.mechanism: A mature EMA-separated trend produces a range expansion that closes through the prior bar in the opposite direction.
Short-horizon ATR is no more than 60% of long-horizon ATR and a completed bar breaks a prior 4-hour range with a directional body.
A strong trend attempts a new local extreme but closes across EMA20 in the opposite direction.
A strong EMA-separated trend retraces to EMA20 and a completed bar closes back in the trend direction.
Distinct fixed mechanisms: London opening-range expansion, half-yen round-number rejection, and once-daily four-day time-series momentum.

scientific_boundary: Variants are distinct mechanisms or reference levels, not parameter-grid cells. Thresholds and horizons are frozen before outcome computation.
